title: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer (PCDOE) practice questions

exams.name: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: A company wants separate policies and billing visibility for production, staging, and development across many teams. What hierarchy fits?
options: An organization with folders per environment (and optionally per team), each containing projects
questions.correct_rationale: Folders group projects so IAM and org policies can be applied per environment.
questions.distractor_summary: A single project mixes environments, many organizations are hard to manage, and labels do not enforce policy.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: Which resource is the root of the Google Cloud resource hierarchy?
questions.correct_rationale: The organization node sits above folders and projects.
questions.distractor_summary: Projects and folders sit below it, and VPCs are resources inside projects.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: Teams need their own projects, but a central team must control networking. What design fits?
options: Every team creates its own unconnected VPC with public IPs
Shared VPC with a host project managed by the network team and service projects owned by application teams
VPN between every pair of projects
questions.correct_rationale: Shared VPC centralizes network control while teams own workloads.
questions.distractor_summary: Unconnected VPCs and public IPs fragment the network, one project mixes teams, and pairwise VPNs do not scale.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: Where should IAM bindings for an entire environment be granted to reduce repetition?
options: At the folder that contains the environment's projects
questions.correct_rationale: Folder-level bindings are inherited by all projects in the folder.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-resource grants repeat work, VM metadata is not IAM, and README files do not grant access.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: A company wants a repeatable, secure landing zone created as code. What should it use?
options: Manual console clicks recorded in screenshots
The Google Cloud enterprise foundations blueprint or Fabric FAST deployed with Terraform
One shared Owner account for setup
A single project for all teams
questions.correct_rationale: Blueprints codify a secure, repeatable organization setup.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual setup drifts, shared accounts lack accountability, and one project does not scale.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.1 Designing the overall resource hierarchy for an organization
questions.question: What is the purpose of the Project Factory approach?
options: Creating projects consistently with standard APIs, IAM, networking, and billing settings through automation
questions.correct_rationale: Project factories standardize project creation.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not build images, test load, or manage DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Infrastructure must be defined as code with state stored safely for a team. What should be used?
options: Terraform with local state files on laptops
Terraform with a Cloud Storage backend for remote state with object versioning
questions.correct_rationale: Remote state in Cloud Storage supports team collaboration and history.
questions.distractor_summary: Local state causes conflicts, console changes lack code, and hard-coded scripts are brittle.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: What does Infrastructure Manager provide?
options: A managed service that runs Terraform to deploy and manage Google Cloud resources
questions.correct_rationale: Infrastructure Manager automates Terraform deployments with Google-managed execution.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a registry, log tool, or DNS service.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Infrastructure changes must be reviewed before they are applied, with the plan visible in the pull request. What design fits?
options: Engineers run terraform apply from their laptops
Apply changes first and review later
A CI pipeline that runs terraform plan on pull requests and terraform apply after merge, with approvals
questions.correct_rationale: Plan-on-PR and apply-after-merge keep changes reviewed.
questions.distractor_summary: Laptop applies bypass review, and late review or skipped plans risk mistakes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: What is Config Connector used for?
options: Managing Google Cloud resources through Kubernetes resource manifests
questions.correct_rationale: Config Connector lets Kubernetes manage cloud resources declaratively.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not query data, scan images, or host sites.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Configuration of many GKE clusters must stay consistent and synced from Git. What should be used?
options: Config Sync (GitOps) from a Git repository
Manual kubectl apply on each cluster
questions.correct_rationale: Config Sync continuously reconciles clusters with Git.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual applies, email, and console edits drift.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: What is configuration drift?
options: Differences between the actual infrastructure state and the state defined in code
questions.correct_rationale: Drift happens when manual changes bypass IaC.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not latency, billing, or restarts.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Terraform modules are shared across teams. How should versions be managed?
options: Always use the latest commit on main
Copy module code into each repo without versions
Edit shared modules directly in production
Publish modules with semantic version tags in a registry or Git, and pin versions in callers
questions.correct_rationale: Pinned versions make upgrades deliberate and safe.
questions.distractor_summary: Floating on main, unversioned copies, and direct edits cause surprises.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Which tool converts existing Google Cloud resources into Terraform configuration?
options: gcloud resource-config bulk-export with Terraform format
questions.correct_rationale: Bulk export can generate Terraform for existing resources.
questions.distractor_summary: SSH, copy, and logs commands do not export configuration.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: A team wants a managed CI service on Google Cloud that builds containers from Git commits. What should it use?
options: Cloud Build with triggers connected to the repository
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Build runs build steps in containers and supports Git triggers.
questions.distractor_summary: Scheduler, CDN, and Memorystore are not CI services.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: What does Cloud Deploy provide?
options: Managed continuous delivery with delivery pipelines, targets, releases, and promotions to GKE, Cloud Run, and other runtimes
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Deploy manages progressive delivery across targets.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not source hosting, log analysis, or DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: Builds must reach private resources in a VPC, such as an internal artifact server. What should be used?
options: Cloud Build private pools connected to the VPC
Default Cloud Build pools with public IP allowlists
questions.correct_rationale: Private pools run in a peered network that can reach private resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Default pools lack VPC access, public servers add risk, and laptops are not CI.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: Where should built container images be stored on Google Cloud?
questions.correct_rationale: Artifact Registry stores containers and language packages.
questions.distractor_summary: SQL, DNS, and Logging are not image stores.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: A company uses GitHub Actions and wants to deploy to Google Cloud without service account keys. What should be configured?
options: A long-lived service account key in GitHub secrets
A personal access token for a Google user
Workload Identity Federation with GitHub's OIDC provider
questions.correct_rationale: Federation exchanges GitHub tokens for short-lived Google credentials.
questions.distractor_summary: Keys and personal tokens are long-lived, and public buckets are unsafe.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: What does a Cloud Build configuration file (cloudbuild.yaml) define?
options: The build steps, each running in a container, plus options like images and substitutions
questions.correct_rationale: cloudbuild.yaml describes the build pipeline.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not define firewalls, org policies, or billing.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: Applications run on GKE in Google Cloud and on clusters in another cloud. They need a consistent deployment model. What fits?
options: GKE Enterprise fleet management with Config Sync and a common CI/CD pipeline
questions.correct_rationale: Fleet tools give consistent management across environments.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual per-cloud processes drift, and the other choices are not CI/CD.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.3 Designing a CI/CD architecture stack in Google Cloud, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments
questions.question: Which Cloud Deploy feature lets a release be promoted only after approval?
questions.correct_rationale: Targets can require approval before rollouts proceed.
questions.distractor_summary: Profiles, substitutions, and analysis do not approve rollouts.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Development, staging, and production must have the same infrastructure with different sizes. How should this be done?
options: Write separate code for each environment by hand
Use the same IaC modules with per-environment variable files or workspaces
questions.correct_rationale: Shared modules with different inputs keep environments consistent.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate code drifts, partial IaC leaves gaps, and manual copies are error-prone.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Why should production and non-production run in separate projects?
options: Because projects cannot hold more than one service
To isolate access, quotas, billing, and blast radius
questions.correct_rationale: Separate projects limit impact and simplify access control.
questions.distractor_summary: Projects can hold many services, and isolation is not meant to complicate IAM or add latency.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: Developers need short-lived preview environments for each pull request. What approach fits?
options: One shared environment that all PRs overwrite
Pipelines that create ephemeral resources, such as a Cloud Run revision with a tag or a namespace, and delete them after merge
Manual setup that is never cleaned up
questions.correct_rationale: Ephemeral environments give isolated testing with automatic cleanup.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared overwrites conflict, production previews are risky, and manual setups leak cost.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.question: What are Skaffold profiles used for with Cloud Deploy?
options: Applying different rendering settings, such as manifests or values, for each target environment
questions.correct_rationale: Profiles let one Skaffold config adapt to each environment.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not encrypt, manage IAM, or manage DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.5 Designing and managing secure cloud development environments
questions.question: Developers need secure, managed development environments in Google Cloud with no source code on laptops. What should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Workstations provide managed dev environments in a VPC.
questions.distractor_summary: Public shared VMs are insecure, and CDN and Scheduler are not dev environments.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.5 Designing and managing secure cloud development environments
questions.question: What does Gemini Code Assist provide to developers?
options: AI-powered code completion and help in IDEs, with enterprise controls
questions.correct_rationale: Code Assist helps developers write and understand code.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a firewall, database, or load balancer.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.5 Designing and managing secure cloud development environments
questions.question: Cloud Workstations must not allow copying source code to the internet. What controls help?
options: Private workstation clusters, VPC Service Controls, and restricted egress through firewall rules
questions.correct_rationale: Private networking and perimeters limit data exfiltration.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs, no logs, and shared access increase risk.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Bootstrapping and maintaining a Google Cloud organization
questions.subdomain: 1.5 Designing and managing secure cloud development environments
questions.question: Why should developer tools authenticate with user credentials or impersonation rather than service account keys?
options: Keys never expire, which is safer
It avoids long-lived keys and keeps actions tied to a person in audit logs
questions.correct_rationale: User credentials and impersonation are auditable and short-lived.
questions.distractor_summary: Keys are not safer, and impersonation is logged.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A team wants every commit to main to build, test, and produce a deployable image automatically. What should be configured?
options: A manual build once a week
A Cloud Build trigger on pushes to main that runs tests and pushes the image to Artifact Registry
A Cloud Scheduler job that emails developers
questions.correct_rationale: Triggers automate CI on every change.
questions.distractor_summary: Weekly manual builds, emails, and laptop builds do not provide CI.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is the main difference between continuous delivery and continuous deployment?
options: Continuous delivery keeps code always releasable with a manual approval to release, while continuous deployment releases every passing change automatically
questions.correct_rationale: Both automate the pipeline, but only continuous deployment removes the manual release step.
questions.distractor_summary: They differ, continuous deployment does deploy, and continuous delivery still tests.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A pipeline must deploy the same image to staging and production, with production requiring sign-off. What should be used?
options: Cloud Deploy with a delivery pipeline of staging then production targets, and approval required on production
Manually copy the image between registries
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Deploy promotes the same release through targets with approvals.
questions.distractor_summary: Rebuilding risks differences, deploying production first is backward, and manual copying is error-prone.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is a Cloud Deploy release?
options: An immutable snapshot of rendered manifests for a specific build, ready to roll out to targets
questions.correct_rationale: Releases tie a build to manifests for promotion.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a branch, firewall, or billing account.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A build pipeline should run unit tests in parallel with linting to save time. How can this be done in Cloud Build?
options: Run all steps strictly in sequence
Use waitFor in build steps so independent steps start at the same time
Use a larger Cloud SQL instance
questions.correct_rationale: waitFor controls step dependencies and allows parallelism.
questions.distractor_summary: Sequential runs are slower, separate projects add overhead, and Cloud SQL is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which Cloud Build feature lets you reuse a build file with different values, such as an image tag?
questions.correct_rationale: Substitutions inject variable values into builds.
questions.distractor_summary: Pools set where builds run, and approvals gate builds.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Builds must be blocked until a release manager approves for sensitive repositories. What feature fits?
options: Cloud Build approval required on the trigger
questions.correct_rationale: Approval-gated triggers wait for a human decision.
questions.distractor_summary: Timeouts, steps, and machine types do not add approval.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What does Skaffold do in a Cloud Deploy pipeline?
options: Renders manifests and handles deployment logic for each target
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Deploy uses Skaffold for rendering and deploying.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not store secrets, scan images, or manage DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A team uses GitHub for code and wants Cloud Build to run on pull requests. What should be configured?
options: Copy code manually into Cloud Build
Use Cloud Scheduler to poll GitHub
Email diffs to the build system
Connect the GitHub repository to Cloud Build and create a pull request trigger
questions.correct_rationale: Repository connections and PR triggers run builds on pull requests.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual copies, polling, and emails are not integrations.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is trunk-based development?
options: Developers keep long-lived branches for months
Developers merge small changes into a main branch frequently, with short-lived branches and feature flags
Developers work only on release branches
questions.correct_rationale: Trunk-based development supports fast, continuous integration.
questions.distractor_summary: Long branches, no merges, and release-only work slow integration.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A pipeline takes 40 minutes because dependencies are downloaded every time. What should be improved?
options: Cache dependencies, for example by storing them in Cloud Storage or using Kaniko layer caching, and reuse base images
questions.correct_rationale: Caching cuts repeated downloads and build time.
questions.distractor_summary: More steps and smaller machines slow builds, and disabling tests lowers quality.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is a build artifact?
options: The output of a build, such as a container image or binary, that is stored and deployed
questions.correct_rationale: Artifacts are the deployable outputs of builds.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not comments, firewall rules, or reports.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Infrastructure code must be validated on every pull request. What should the pipeline do?
options: Run terraform fmt, validate, and plan, plus policy checks, and post results to the pull request
questions.correct_rationale: Automated checks catch issues before merging.
questions.distractor_summary: Direct applies, skipped checks, and monthly validation increase risk.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which tool can scan Terraform plans against organization policies before apply?
options: gcloud terraform vet with policy libraries
questions.correct_rationale: terraform vet checks plans against constraints.
questions.distractor_summary: SSH, top, and ls do not check policy.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A Cloud Run service must be updated without downtime, and traffic must shift gradually to the new revision. What should be used?
options: Change the service name each time
Deploy a new revision with no traffic, then split traffic gradually between revisions
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Run traffic splitting supports gradual rollout.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting or stopping causes downtime, and renaming breaks clients.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which Cloud Deploy strategy rolls out a new version to a percentage of traffic first?
questions.correct_rationale: Canary deployments shift traffic in phases.
questions.distractor_summary: Standard deploys fully, and the others are not Cloud Deploy strategies.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A canary release on GKE shows higher error rates. What should happen?
options: Stop the rollout and roll back to the previous release, then investigate
questions.correct_rationale: Canaries exist to catch problems before full rollout.
questions.distractor_summary: Promoting spreads errors, ignoring them hurts users, and deleting the cluster is drastic.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What does a blue/green deployment need?
options: Two environments, one serving traffic and one with the new version, and a way to switch traffic between them
No load balancer or routing control
questions.correct_rationale: Blue/green relies on switching traffic quickly between environments.
questions.distractor_summary: One environment cannot do blue/green, routing control is needed, and slow DNS defeats the purpose.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A rollback is needed after a bad Cloud Deploy rollout. What is the quickest method?
options: Roll back the target to the previous successful release in Cloud Deploy
Rebuild the old version from source
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Deploy can redeploy a previous release.
questions.distractor_summary: Rebuilding takes longer, deleting targets breaks pipelines, and waiting prolongs impact.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which GKE deployment setting controls how many pods can be unavailable during a rolling update?
questions.correct_rationale: maxUnavailable and maxSurge control rolling update pace.
questions.distractor_summary: The other settings do not control rollout pace.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Database schema changes must be released with application changes without downtime. What pattern fits?
options: Drop old columns before deploying the app
Stop the app and change the schema during business hours
Expand and contract: add backward-compatible schema changes first, deploy the app, then remove old structures later
questions.correct_rationale: Expand and contract keeps old and new versions working during rollout.
questions.distractor_summary: Dropping first breaks old code, downtime is avoidable, and schemas must evolve.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is a feature flag?
options: A configuration switch that turns functionality on or off without redeploying code
questions.correct_rationale: Feature flags separate deployment from release.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not firewalls, tags, or alerts.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A pipeline must deploy Terraform changes to staging automatically and production after approval. What design fits?
options: One state file for all environments applied at once
Separate apply stages per environment with state per environment and a manual approval before production
questions.correct_rationale: Separate stages and states limit blast radius.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared state mixes environments, production-first is backward, and no approvals increase risk.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which Cloud Run feature tags a revision with a URL for testing before it gets traffic?
questions.correct_rationale: Tags give a revision its own URL without serving main traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Min instances, concurrency, and CPU settings do not create test URLs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Pipelines must deploy to GKE clusters in several regions in order, stopping if a region fails. What fits?
options: A single kubectl apply to all clusters at once
Deploy only to one region forever
A Cloud Deploy pipeline with sequential targets per region, or parallel deployment with a multi-target and verification
questions.correct_rationale: Staged regional rollouts limit impact.
questions.distractor_summary: All-at-once deploys spread failures, manual deploys are error-prone, and one region limits resilience.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What does Cloud Deploy verification do?
options: Runs tests against a target after deployment and marks the rollout failed if they fail
questions.correct_rationale: Verification adds post-deploy checks to rollouts.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt, scan code, or create DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Images must be built from source with a Dockerfile in Cloud Build. Which builder is commonly used?
options: The docker builder image (gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker) or Kaniko
The gcloud builder with no Docker
questions.correct_rationale: Docker and Kaniko build container images in Cloud Build steps.
questions.distractor_summary: gsutil, kubectl, and plain gcloud do not build images.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is immutable infrastructure?
options: Replacing servers or containers with new versions instead of changing them in place
questions.correct_rationale: Immutable deployments reduce drift and make rollbacks easier.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not avoiding changes, manual edits, or single servers.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: A deployment needs automated checks of latency and errors during a canary before promoting. What can be used with Cloud Deploy?
options: Deploy verification or automation rules with metrics checks, such as calling Cloud Monitoring in a verify container
questions.correct_rationale: Automated metric checks make canary decisions reliable.
questions.distractor_summary: Weekly inspection is too slow, and no checks or unit tests alone miss runtime issues.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which Cloud Deploy feature can promote releases automatically when conditions are met?
options: Automation rules, such as promote release and advance rollout
questions.correct_rationale: Automation rules move releases forward without manual steps.
questions.distractor_summary: Profiles, substitutions, and cleanup policies do not promote releases.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: App Engine standard must test a new version with 10 percent of traffic. What should be done?
options: Deploy the new version without promoting, then split traffic 90/10 between versions
questions.correct_rationale: App Engine traffic splitting supports gradual testing.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting the old version removes fallback, new projects are unnecessary, and NAT is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: What is Artifact Registry cleanup policy used for?
options: Deleting old or untagged artifacts automatically to control storage
questions.correct_rationale: Cleanup policies remove artifacts by rules.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not encrypt, build, or grant.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Build steps need a database password. Where should it be stored and how should it be used?
options: In the cloudbuild.yaml file in plain text
In Secret Manager, accessed in Cloud Build through availableSecrets and secretEnv
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Build integrates with Secret Manager securely.
questions.distractor_summary: Plain text, images, and public buckets expose secrets.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 2. Building and implementing CI/CD pipelines for applications and infrastructure
questions.question: Which service account does Cloud Build use to run builds by default?
options: A Cloud Build or Compute Engine service account, depending on project settings, and a user-specified service account is recommended

questions.distractor_summary: Build logs, registries, and NAT do not show service status.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Application logs should be structured so they can be queried by fields. What should the app write?
options: Logs only to local files on disk
JSON-formatted log entries to stdout or through the Cloud Logging client library
questions.correct_rationale: Structured logs map into jsonPayload fields for querying.
questions.distractor_summary: Random text is hard to query, local files may be lost, and screenshots are not logs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Where do GKE container logs go by default?
options: Cloud Logging, through the built-in logging agent
A local file on the developer's laptop
questions.correct_rationale: GKE sends container logs to Cloud Logging by default.
questions.distractor_summary: Logs are collected, not lost, and do not go to laptops or SQL.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Logs from several projects must be analyzed together with SQL. What should be configured?
options: Querying each project separately and merging by hand
A log sink routing logs to a central log bucket upgraded to use Log Analytics, or to BigQuery
questions.correct_rationale: Central buckets with Log Analytics allow SQL across projects.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual merging is slow, disabling logs loses data, and email does not scale.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What does a log-based metric do?
options: Counts or extracts values from log entries to create metrics for charts and alerts
questions.correct_rationale: Log-based metrics turn log events into time series.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not delete, encrypt, or export to Git.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Logs on Compute Engine VMs must be collected along with metrics. What should be installed?
questions.correct_rationale: The Ops Agent collects logs and metrics from VMs.
questions.distractor_summary: SQL Proxy, kubectl, and gsutil do not collect telemetry.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: How can log storage costs be reduced?
options: Increase retention to the maximum everywhere
Use exclusion filters for unneeded logs and set appropriate retention on log buckets
Log every debug message in production
questions.correct_rationale: Exclusions and retention settings control cost.
questions.distractor_summary: Duplication, maximum retention, and verbose logging add cost.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Logs must be retained for years for compliance but rarely read. What is a cost-effective destination?
options: The default log bucket with 30 days retention
A sink to a Cloud Storage bucket with an archive or coldline storage class and a retention policy
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Storage cold classes store long-term logs cheaply.
questions.distractor_summary: Short default retention misses requirements, and local disks or laptops are unsafe.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Which Logging query finds error entries from a specific Cloud Run service?
questions.correct_rationale: Logging query language filters by resource and severity.
questions.distractor_summary: The other commands are not Logging queries.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Developers want to see logs related to a single request across services. What should be done?
options: Include the trace ID in log entries so logs correlate with Cloud Trace spans
Use random IDs in each service
Log only in the front end
questions.correct_rationale: Trace correlation links logs from one request.
questions.distractor_summary: Random IDs break correlation, and partial logging leaves gaps.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What is the purpose of the _Default log bucket?
options: Storing most logs, other than required audit logs, with configurable retention
questions.correct_rationale: _Default holds logs not routed to _Required.
questions.distractor_summary: _Required holds Admin Activity logs, and billing and images are elsewhere.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Sensitive fields appear in application logs. What should be done?
options: Stop logging sensitive data in the app, and restrict access to existing logs with log views
questions.correct_rationale: Fixing the source and restricting access reduce exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: Public logs, longer retention, and ignoring the issue increase risk.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Which tool shows logs from recent errors grouped by stack trace and frequency?
questions.correct_rationale: Error Reporting aggregates and groups application errors.
questions.distractor_summary: Profiler, Scheduler, and CDN do not group errors.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: A team needs custom business metrics, such as orders per minute, in Cloud Monitoring. What should they use?
options: Custom metrics written through OpenTelemetry or the Monitoring API
questions.correct_rationale: Custom metrics bring app-specific data into Monitoring.
questions.distractor_summary: Screenshots, billing, and DNS do not create metrics.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What is Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus?
options: A managed, scalable backend for Prometheus metrics with PromQL queries
questions.correct_rationale: It lets teams use Prometheus without managing storage.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not DNS, an archive, or a registry.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: High-cardinality labels, such as user IDs on metrics, cause cost and performance problems. What should be done?
options: Remove high-cardinality labels from metrics and record such details in logs or traces instead
questions.correct_rationale: Metrics should have bounded label sets.
questions.distractor_summary: More labels or per-user metrics increase cardinality.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What does a metric's alignment period do in Cloud Monitoring?
options: Groups data points into time intervals for aggregation
questions.correct_rationale: Alignment regularizes time series for charts and alerts.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete data, rename metrics, or grant access.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: GKE workloads must expose metrics scraped by Prometheus format. How can they be collected in Google Cloud?
options: Enable managed collection and create PodMonitoring resources for the workloads
questions.correct_rationale: Managed collection scrapes Prometheus endpoints in GKE.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual copying is impractical, and NAT or disabling metrics do not help.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What is OpenTelemetry?
options: An open standard and set of SDKs for collecting traces, metrics, and logs
questions.correct_rationale: OpenTelemetry provides vendor-neutral telemetry instrumentation.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a database, firewall, or billing format.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Monitoring must cover metrics from many projects in one place. What should be configured?
options: Separate dashboards in every project with no central view
A scoping project with a metrics scope that includes the monitored projects
questions.correct_rationale: Metrics scopes let one project view metrics from many.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate views, spreadsheets, and disabled monitoring do not centralize.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Which metric type represents a value that can go up and down, such as current memory usage?
questions.correct_rationale: Gauges measure a value at a point in time.
questions.distractor_summary: Cumulative metrics only increase, delta represents change, and string is not a metric kind here.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: A team wants to know whether their service's CPU is near saturation over time. Which chart is most helpful?
options: A pie chart of team members
A time series of CPU utilization against the limit, with percentiles across instances
questions.correct_rationale: Time series with limits show saturation trends.
questions.distractor_summary: The other choices do not show CPU usage.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Why are latency percentiles such as p95 and p99 more useful than averages?
options: They are always lower than averages
They show the experience of slower requests, which averages hide
questions.correct_rationale: Tail latency affects real users.
questions.distractor_summary: Percentiles can be higher than averages and include slow requests.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: On-call engineers need a dashboard showing the golden signals for a service. What should be built?
options: A wiki page with text only
A Cloud Monitoring custom dashboard with latency, traffic, errors, and saturation charts
questions.correct_rationale: Dashboards give a live view of key signals.
questions.distractor_summary: Slides, text pages, and billing reports are not live.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: What is an alerting policy in Cloud Monitoring?
options: A set of conditions and notification channels that create incidents when conditions are met
questions.correct_rationale: Alerting policies define when and how to notify.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not firewalls, budgets, or branches.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Alerts fire when CPU briefly spikes, waking engineers for no user impact. What should be changed?
options: Alert on user-facing symptoms such as SLO burn rate, and use durations and thresholds that ignore brief spikes
questions.correct_rationale: Symptom-based alerts reduce noise.
questions.distractor_summary: Immediate spike alerts add noise, no alerts miss problems, and paging everyone causes fatigue.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Which notification channels can Cloud Monitoring use?
options: Email, SMS, mobile app, Slack, PagerDuty, webhooks, and Pub/Sub
questions.correct_rationale: Monitoring supports many notification channels.
questions.distractor_summary: Fax and postal mail are not channels, and channels do exist.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: A team wants to check that a public website responds from several regions every minute. What should be configured?
options: An uptime check with an alerting policy
questions.correct_rationale: Uptime checks probe endpoints from multiple locations.
questions.distractor_summary: Exclusions, builds, and NAT do not test availability.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: What does an alert's documentation field provide?
options: Guidance for responders, such as runbook links, included in notifications
questions.correct_rationale: Documentation helps responders act quickly.
questions.distractor_summary: Thresholds and data are separate, and billing is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Alerts should be suppressed during a planned maintenance window. What can be used?
options: Snooze the relevant alert policies for the window
questions.correct_rationale: Snoozing pauses notifications temporarily.
questions.distractor_summary: Deleting or disabling loses coverage, and ignoring notifications is unsafe.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Which language can be used to write alert conditions over Prometheus-style metrics in Cloud Monitoring?
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Monitoring supports PromQL for queries and alert conditions.
questions.distractor_summary: SQL, HCL, and YAML alone are not the query language here.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Dashboards must be version-controlled and deployed consistently across projects. What should be done?
options: Define dashboards as JSON and deploy them with Terraform or the Monitoring API
Recreate them by hand in each project
Keep them only in personal favorites
questions.correct_rationale: Dashboards as code are repeatable and reviewable.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual recreation drifts, and screenshots or favorites are not deployable.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: What is a burn rate in SLO alerting?
options: How fast the error budget is being consumed compared with the rate that would exactly use it by the end of the window
questions.correct_rationale: Burn rate shows how quickly the budget is being spent.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not temperature, cost, or deployments.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A Cloud Run service returns 503 errors under load. What should be checked first?
options: Instance limits, concurrency settings, startup time, and whether max instances is reached
questions.correct_rationale: Capacity and scaling settings commonly cause 503s under load.
questions.distractor_summary: Commits, billing names, and registrars do not cause 503s.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A GKE pod is in CrashLoopBackOff. What should be checked first?
options: The container logs and the previous container's exit reason with kubectl logs --previous and kubectl describe pod
questions.correct_rationale: Logs and pod events explain crashes.
questions.distractor_summary: Billing, DNS, and org policies rarely explain container crashes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A GKE pod is stuck in Pending. What is a likely cause?
options: Not enough node resources, unsatisfied node selectors or affinity, or missing persistent volumes
The service has too many labels
The cluster has too many namespaces
questions.correct_rationale: Pending pods usually cannot be scheduled.
questions.distractor_summary: Image size, labels, and namespaces do not usually block scheduling.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool helps check whether a firewall rule blocks traffic between two VMs?
options: Connectivity Tests in Network Intelligence Center
questions.correct_rationale: Connectivity Tests analyze configuration and show where packets would be dropped.
questions.distractor_summary: Profiler, Error Reporting, and Scheduler do not test network paths.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A VM cannot reach the internet, and it has no external IP. What should be checked?
options: Whether Cloud NAT is configured for the subnet and the route to the default internet gateway exists, plus egress firewall rules
questions.correct_rationale: Private VMs need Cloud NAT and routes for internet access.
questions.distractor_summary: Disk size, billing names, and labels do not affect connectivity.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A pod reports ImagePullBackOff. What is a likely cause?
options: The pod has too much memory
The image name or tag is wrong, or the node's service account lacks permission to pull from Artifact Registry
questions.correct_rationale: Pull failures come from bad references or missing permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Memory, autoscaling, and HTTPS do not cause pull errors.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A deployment works in staging but fails in production with permission denied errors. What should be compared?
options: The service accounts and IAM roles, org policies, and VPC Service Controls in each environment
questions.correct_rationale: Permission differences between environments cause such failures.
questions.distractor_summary: Dashboard colors, team size, and retention are unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool can show the full request path and timing across microservices to locate slow calls?
questions.correct_rationale: Trace shows spans and latency for each service call.
questions.distractor_summary: Scheduler, DNS, and registries do not trace requests.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: An app uses too much CPU in production, and the team wants to find which functions are responsible with low overhead. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: Profiler samples CPU and memory use by function in production.
questions.distractor_summary: Trace shows latency, Error Reporting groups errors, and uptime checks test availability.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool lets you open an interactive shell in the browser with gcloud and kubectl preinstalled?
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Shell provides a browser terminal with tools.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, NAT, and Armor are not shells.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A Compute Engine VM does not boot after a change. How can the team see boot messages?
options: View the serial port output, or connect through the interactive serial console if enabled
questions.correct_rationale: Serial output shows boot logs even when SSH fails.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN logs, billing, and registries do not show boot output.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool provides insights into firewall rule usage, such as shadowed or unused rules?
options: Firewall Insights in Network Intelligence Center
questions.correct_rationale: Firewall Insights analyzes rule effectiveness.
questions.distractor_summary: Profiler, Trace, and Build do not analyze firewalls.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Engineers want to debug a GKE workload interactively without changing its image. What can they use?
options: Rebuild the image with debugging tools for every issue
kubectl debug with an ephemeral debug container
questions.correct_rationale: Ephemeral containers attach tools to running pods.
questions.distractor_summary: Rebuilding every time is slow, deletion is destructive, and CDN is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool records and analyzes VPC network performance and topology across projects?
questions.correct_rationale: Network Intelligence Center includes topology, performance, and connectivity tools.
questions.distractor_summary: The others are unrelated services.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A service has intermittent latency spikes that do not show in averages. What should the team examine?
options: Latency distributions and traces for the slow requests, along with logs at those times
questions.correct_rationale: Distributions and traces reveal tail latency causes.
questions.distractor_summary: Averages hide spikes, and billing or Git logs do not explain latency.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: VMs are consistently using 15 percent of their CPU. What should be done?
options: Apply rightsizing recommendations to move to smaller machine types
questions.correct_rationale: Rightsizing reduces waste for underused VMs.
questions.distractor_summary: Bigger machines and more VMs add waste.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: What are committed use discounts (CUDs)?
options: Discounts for using preemptible VMs only
Discounts for committing to a level of resource use or spend for one or three years
questions.correct_rationale: CUDs lower prices for steady workloads.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not free, not limited to Spot VMs, and not penalties.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A batch job can tolerate interruptions and must be as cheap as possible. Which VM option fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Spot VMs are heavily discounted but can be preempted.
questions.distractor_summary: Commitments suit steady use, sole-tenant nodes cost more, and larger machines add cost.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: What do sustained use discounts provide?
options: Automatic discounts for running certain Compute Engine resources for a large part of the month
questions.correct_rationale: Sustained use discounts apply automatically to eligible resources.
questions.distractor_summary: No contract is needed, and they do not apply only to storage or idle resources.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: GKE costs are high because nodes are underused. What can help?
options: Use cluster autoscaler, right-size requests, consider GKE Autopilot, and review GKE cost allocation
questions.correct_rationale: Autoscaling and accurate requests improve bin packing.
questions.distractor_summary: More nodes, no autoscaling, and high requests add waste.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool shows cost breakdowns by project, service, and label?
options: Cloud Billing reports and billing export to BigQuery
questions.correct_rationale: Billing reports and exports show cost details.
questions.distractor_summary: Trace, Profiler, and Error Reporting do not show costs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Teams must be alerted when spending in a project exceeds a threshold. What should be configured?
options: A Cloud Billing budget with alert thresholds and notifications, optionally to Pub/Sub for automation
questions.correct_rationale: Budgets track spending against thresholds.
questions.distractor_summary: CPU alerts, exclusions, and firewalls do not watch spend.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which feature recommends deleting idle resources, such as unattached disks or idle VMs?
questions.correct_rationale: Recommender finds idle resources that can be removed.
questions.distractor_summary: Trace, Build, and Armor do not recommend cleanup.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: A team wants to receive a notification when a specific error message appears in logs. What should be configured?
options: A log-based alerting policy that matches the message
questions.correct_rationale: Log-based alerts notify on matching log entries.
questions.distractor_summary: Uptime checks, budgets, and firewalls do not watch log text.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: What does the Cloud Logging "Log Router" do?
options: Routes incoming log entries to destinations through sinks, applying inclusion and exclusion filters
questions.correct_rationale: The Log Router decides where logs are stored.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not route packets, DNS, or email.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Audit logs must be streamed to a third-party SIEM in near real time. What should be configured?
options: A Cloud Storage sink read once a month
A log sink to Pub/Sub, with the SIEM subscribing to the topic
questions.correct_rationale: Pub/Sub sinks deliver logs quickly to external tools.
questions.distractor_summary: Daily or monthly exports are slow, and screenshots are not integrations.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: Which tool collects metrics and traces from applications using OpenTelemetry and sends them to Google Cloud?
options: The OpenTelemetry Collector or SDK exporters for Google Cloud
questions.correct_rationale: OpenTelemetry exporters send telemetry to Cloud Monitoring and Trace.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Armor, and NAT do not collect telemetry.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.question: A team needs to monitor Cloud SQL query performance. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: Query Insights shows slow queries and load by query.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN logs, registries, and Scheduler do not analyze queries.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: What is the purpose of incident auto-close in Cloud Monitoring alerting?
options: Closing incidents automatically after the condition is no longer met for a period
questions.correct_rationale: Auto-close keeps incident lists tidy.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete policies, disable notifications, or create projects.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Alerting must route database alerts to the database team and app alerts to the app team. What should be configured?
options: Separate alert policies with notification channels for each team, using labels for routing where supported
questions.correct_rationale: Targeted channels send alerts to the right owners.
questions.distractor_summary: Emailing everyone causes noise, and no channels or dashboard-only alerts are missed.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 4. Implementing observability practices
questions.subdomain: 4.3 Managing dashboards and alerts in Cloud Monitoring
questions.question: Which Cloud Monitoring feature combines multiple conditions in one alert policy?
options: Multi-condition policies with AND or OR combiners
questions.correct_rationale: Policies can combine conditions.
questions.distractor_summary: Exclusions, budgets, and regions do not combine alert conditions.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A Cloud Build step fails with permission denied when pushing an image. What should be checked?
options: That the image is small enough
That the build has more steps
That the build service account has Artifact Registry Writer on the repository
questions.correct_rationale: Pushing requires write permission on the repository.
questions.distractor_summary: Size, public access, and step count do not grant permission.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: An HTTP load balancer marks all backends unhealthy. What is a common cause?
options: The backends have too much memory
Firewall rules do not allow health check ranges 35.191.0.0/16 and 130.211.0.0/22, or the health check path is wrong
questions.correct_rationale: Health checks need firewall access and a correct path.
questions.distractor_summary: Memory, labels, and HTTPS are not typical causes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: A GKE service is reachable inside the cluster but not through an Ingress. What should be checked?
options: The Ingress backend health checks, service type and ports, and readiness probe path
questions.correct_rationale: Ingress depends on healthy backends and correct service configuration.
questions.distractor_summary: Billing, org policies, and namespace counts are unlikely causes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which tool shows latency between Google Cloud regions and zones to help separate network issues from application issues?
options: Performance Dashboard in Network Intelligence Center
questions.correct_rationale: Performance Dashboard shows packet loss and latency across Google's network.
questions.distractor_summary: Scheduler, Secret Manager, and Build do not measure network performance.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Cloud Run services are idle at night but still cost money. What setting should be checked?
options: Minimum instances, which keep instances warm and billed even when idle
questions.correct_rationale: Setting min instances to zero lets the service scale to zero.
questions.distractor_summary: Request size, ports, and names do not keep instances running.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: Which Cloud Storage feature moves objects to cheaper storage classes automatically based on access patterns?
questions.correct_rationale: Autoclass transitions objects based on access.
questions.distractor_summary: UBLA, signed URLs, and requester pays do not change classes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud DevOps Engineer
questions.domain: 5. Optimizing performance and troubleshooting
questions.question: BigQuery costs spike due to large ad hoc queries. What controls can help?
options: Partition and cluster tables, set maximum bytes billed, use editions with slot reservations or quotas, and review expensive queries
Run queries with SELECT * on all tables
questions.correct_rationale: These controls limit scanned data and spending.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing limits, disabling partitions, and SELECT * raise costs.
